source.title: Multi-Way Representation Alignment
source.authors: Akshit Achara; Tatiana Gaintseva; Mat'eo Mahaut; Pritish Chakraborty; Viktor Johansson; Melih Barsbey; E. Rodolà; Donato Crisostomi

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The abstract begins with a stray “X” and some figure/table formatting is flattened, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether explicit mappings between representation spaces support cross-model retrieval and stitching, using multi-way GPA and GCPA rather than testing whether naturally occurring alignment rises with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The study tests learned interoperability, not convergence as models become larger or more capable. The authors’ background claims about representations resembling one another cite prior work and are not this study’s results. Rows below focus on held-out retrieval after fitted alignments and the weak-link probing results. Other reported clustering, geometry, noise, and computational results are not recorded as rows because they do not directly measure the tested V4 mapping/interchangeability outcome here.
record.test_reason: A methods paper on multi-way alignment that still reports whether simple orthogonal or linear maps make independently trained, different encoders interchangeable. Unaligned retrieval between TED-MULTI language encoders is near zero; pairwise Procrustes gives 0.43–0.57 rank-1 and GCCA/GPA similar. It also reports a gap to a natively paired model (Flickr30k post-hoc 0.70–0.75 R@1 vs CLIP 0.863). That bears on V4's 'mapped with little loss'. Most rows, however, rank the authors' GCPA against baselines. No scaling, seed, feature-universality or metric-sensitivity test, so the other versions are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a shared multi-way universe makes translation among many models scalable and cycle-consistent. GPA preserves geometry but lags GCCA on retrieval, while GCPA gives state-of-the-art any-to-any retrieval. GPA is the safer reference when the consensus is weak. They do not claim to test convergence itself; the Platonic hypothesis is motivation only.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits supervised multi-way shared-universe mappings (GPA, GCCA, and GCPA) and evaluates held-out retrieval and probing. It does not reproduce a scale-dependent convergence measurement from the cited Platonic Representation Hypothesis work.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with the number and composition of aligned spaces, modality, correspondence quality, and whether the multi-model consensus is reliable. The paper reports GCPA can be unstable for a weakly supported consensus and that retrieval difficulty increases as more language spaces are included.

fits_no_version.finding: Encoders trained on Canny edge maps show lower cosine agreement with the consensus of a universe built from RGB models (0.60–0.74 vs 0.77–0.86 for RGB counterparts) and slightly degrade it. Model capacity alone does not predict agreement or usefulness (Table 14).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment of a model with a multi-model consensus depends on its training data distribution more than on its capacity.

record.problems: The study evaluates post-hoc, correspondence-supervised alignment rather than naturally emerging representational convergence or its relation to model scale/capability. Some main retrieval comparisons are presented in figures without complete numerical values in the supplied text. Table 9's printed GCPA estimates conflict with the accompanying prose claim that GCPA is above GCCA on all three experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the remaining Figure 4, Figure 6, and Figure 7 retrieval breakdowns, Table 8 Flickr30k metrics, and additional reported alignment analyses to keep the record focused on selected held-out mapping outcomes. Figures 2–7 and Tables 8–11 contain further results; the paper text does not provide all plotted pairwise values numerically. Table 9's additional metrics beyond those retained are not extracted.

untested.parts: No comparison of alignment against model size or capability.
Cross-modal retrieval after fitted maps only. No test of whether image–text alignment rises as the models improve.

Untested approaches: relative representations, mapping without paired data, and trained stitching layers. The only measured stitching is linear probes transferred via orthogonal maps. No native within-model reference except the Flickr30k CLIP comparison.
No interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
No variation of the similarity measure or neighbourhood settings. Corruption experiments perturb the fitting data, not the convergence metric.
No test of plateau, or of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment.

missing.what: Post-hoc image–text alignment reaches ~0.70–0.75 R@1 vs CLIP-B/16 0.863 R@1 on the same split. Also Table 8: PW R@1 0.602, GPA 0.601, GCCA 0.626, GCPA 0.640 (clean).
Flickr8k pairwise retrieval: HuBERT→DINOv2 only 14–15% after PW/GPA, HuBERT→CLIP 32% (GPA). Shows weak linear mappability for audio↔vision.
Cross-architecture CIFAR-100 probing transfer via orthogonal maps (PW, GPA-ADD, GPA-REFIT), plus 20-model universe final accuracy 0.626 (GPA-ADD). No native-probe reference is given.
A weak pair improves monotonically in stitching accuracy as clean anchor models are added to the universe.

record.verdict_notes: The reader misread Table 9's flattened columns. GCCA is deterministic, so the values with confidence intervals are GCPA's, and GCPA is above GCCA, matching the prose; the claimed conflict is an extraction error. MARKET-1501 spaces are camera views, not different models. Most rows compare the authors' GCPA with baselines; only the NA vs PW/GPA/GCCA contrasts and the CLIP gap bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep or comparison of representation alignment against model size or capability.
The study evaluates cross-modal retrieval, but does not test whether image–caption alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison of features or shared subspaces across random initializations of the same architecture.

Tests fitted mappings using available correspondences and reports retrieval or stitching outcomes. Does not test relative representations, mapping without paired data, or all the mapping approaches named in the version.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.

The study compares alignment objectives and reports several task metrics, but does not test whether convergence findings vanish under alternative similarity measures or choices such as neighbourhood count or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether natural alignment plateaus or whether shared training data/objectives explain it.

relationships.condition: TED-MULTI, three language-specific BERT-family encoders (M=3), pairwise Procrustes / GPA / GCCA
relationships.reason: Linear or orthogonal maps raise cross-encoder rank-1 retrieval from near zero (r1) to 0.57–0.64 on average (r2–r5).
relationships.display_finding: Linear or orthogonal alignment raised average rank-1 retrieval from near zero to 0.57–0.64.

relationships.condition: TED-MULTI worst pairs and larger sets (M=5, M=10)
relationships.reason: Mapped retrieval falls to 0.43–0.50 on average and 0.23–0.42 on the worst pair (r14–r25), so the maps are far from lossless for some encoder pairs.
relationships.display_finding: With 5 or 10 models, mapped retrieval averaged 0.43–0.50 and fell to 0.23–0.42 for the worst pair.

relationships.condition: ResNet-50/ViT-B/16 pair with Canny-corrupted fitting data, no anchors
relationships.reason: Mapped probing accuracy is 0.57–0.72 at 50–75% corruption (r26–r31) and collapses to near chance at 100% (r32–r34). Interchangeability depends on the data used to fit the map.
relationships.display_finding: Mapped probing accuracy was 0.57–0.72 with 50–75% Canny corruption and collapsed to near chance at 100% corruption.

relationships.condition: Flickr30k, independently trained image and text encoders (from text; no row)
relationships.reason: Text, not rows: post-hoc maps reach about 0.70–0.75 R@1 vs 0.863 for natively paired CLIP-B/16. This is a clear loss relative to joint training.
relationships.display_finding: Post-hoc alignment reached about 0.70–0.75 R@1 on Flickr30k, below 0.863 for jointly trained CLIP-B/16.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: All reported alignment approaches produce held-out retrieval scores, with GCPA highest for both average and worst-pair scores at each listed M; see r2–r25. The paper also describes unaligned retrieval as near zero in r1.
